seam.detail: two repositories; the consumer installs the provider from the registry at the provider's base-commit version. No file removed, no path mounted, no leak check.

lanes.runtime: solo, own container, own branch, no channel; provider repository whole and unmodified
assumptions: repairing its own callers is enough -- it repaired both, core/checks.ts and core/compile.ts, unprompted
zod's public multipleOf behaviour is therefore unchanged and zod's own full suite is green

lanes.runtime: solo, own container, own branch, no channel; consumer repository with the provider from the registry
assumptions: uses zod's own helper deliberately so a form hint and the schema validating the same field cannot disagree

git_outcome.note: the two patches are in different repositories; there is no shared path for git to conflict on

product_outcome.note: integrated = consumer's graded tests with the provider rebuilt from lane A's patch, packed, and installed over the registry copy

stealth.why: lane A's patch leaves the provider repository's own full suite green, and lane B's branch is green against the published provider; neither branch's CI reports anything

convention_graders.note: no migration, route or config surface in either repository

prediction.frozen: fires -- core/index.ts does `export * as util`, so floatSafeRemainder is reachable by any consumer of zod/v4/core. A can repair every in-repo caller it likes; a downstream caller of the function itself still breaks.

merge.why: the two patches are in different repositories; there is no shared path for git to conflict on

checkpoints.why: solo runs keep no cross-agent checkpoint stream

matched_control.differs_in: the contract lane A changed is not exported

mechanism_named_by_claim_map.why: chain `hints.ts::isMultipleOf -> core.util.floatSafeRemainder`, plus the published-surface attribute that explains why the provider's own call-site audit could not reach it. This is the episode the map was designed around and it names the mechanism completely.
